body: I also noticed that with a quarkus native image, the temp files even survive a reboot, I guess there is no config for cleaning the temp dir on startup.
@fantasticExecution is it a Quarkus issue or a Netty one? It looks like a Netty one from your writing?

Thanks for the reply @gsmet .

Yes, netty is responsible for the creation of these unwanted temporary files. The decision, if an `InMemoryAttribute`, `MixedAttribute` or `DiskAttribute` is created is controlled via a flag that you normally control in your own code when calling the `DefaultHttpDataFactory.`

I guess the only bug or missing feature in quarkus would be that I find no way of controlling the "useDisk", "checkSize" and "minSize" and "deleteOnExit" values inside the netty factory via quarkus rest-client config and the default values in the netty code lead to the resource leak.
Yeah, we should definitely be deleting these - cc @Sgitario
`deleteOnExit` is on JVM exit or when the call is finished? Because I'm not sure deleting things on exit would be enough to have a healthy behavior.

> deleteOnExit is on JVM exit or when the call is finished

The former, and yes, it's not enough

I agree, have a look at the netty issue:
https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/10351

Deletion on exiting the JVM is not ideal for servers that run a long time and would fill up the map that holds the reference for files to be deleted.

`deleteOnExit` as it is right now deletes both, after the request and on jvm shutdown as I see the netty code.
But per default, `deleteOnExit` is set to false.

That's not a netty issue; that's a Quarkus issue. It would be configurable if the rest client had used the WebClient underneath, but it uses the bare HTTP client. It already instantiates the HttpDataFactory; we just need to define and pass the parameters.
@Sgitario do you plan on looking into this or should I?
I could work on this from tomorrow mid-day, so feel free to go if you can now!
I won't have time for it today, if I can look at it tomorrow morning, I'll let you know
